decisions.reason: The accepted stainless-steel whisk and shaft adaptation do not change the separate spout geometry, orientation, construction, or beverage-quality constraints.
Selecting the proposed off-the-shelf whisk is consistent with the V1 approach but does not change its current prototype priority or spout-specific sourcing policy.
Adapting the selected whisk to the drive shaft does not alter bowl removal, rapid bowl swapping, or bowl-cleaning access.
The whisk selection may support the existing mixing-quality goal, but the source does not change the required smoothness, foam consistency, or target texture.
The source approves a whisk configuration but does not change the splash target or splash-guard policy.
The approved whisk is intended to work with the selected bowls, but the source does not change bowl capacity, form, or size reference.
Whisk selection and shaft attachment do not alter the solenoid valve, gravity-based dispensing, flow behavior, or operation sequence.

The concrete whisk choice is already owned by the whisk-configuration Requirement; it does not change the BOM deliverable obligation or its selection goal, and duplicating the component fact is unnecessary.
The whisk decision has no effect on machine wording, display name, or placard placement.
The source concerns the mixing whisk and drive shaft, not spout removability, flushing, or sanitation of the fluid path.
The accepted component configuration may later be represented in CAD, but the source does not change the system-layout deliverable or established design direction.
The mechanical whisk selection and shaft adaptation do not change the basic electrical wiring-plan deliverable.
